Title: EGFR-sensitive mutations bilateral diffuse lung adenocarcinoma complicated with acute respiratory distress syndrome: A case report
PMID: 
Authors: 

Abstract
EGFR-sensitive mutations bilateral diffuse lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) complicated with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is relatively rare. It is important to consider whether EGFR-TKI can be simultaneously received when treating with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and anti-infective therapy in these patients, and what adverse events should be noted?

Case Presentation
We report a case of EGFR 19 exon-deficient bilateral diffuse LUAD complicated with ARDS. When treated with ECMO and anti-infective therapy, the patient received oral osimertinib anti-tumor therapy simultaneously. The tumor receded, but eventually irreversible thrombocytopenia developed.

A 48-year-old female patient with no smoking history and disease history developed cough, chest tightness, dyspnea during March 2024, with symptoms gradually worsened. On March 23, 2024, the patient developed fever with temperature up to 38.5°C. Blood routine test (RT) showed leukocytes 6.05 × 109/L, neutrophils 4.34 × 109/L, platelets 331 × 109/L. Chest CT on March 24, 2024, showed multiple nodular and flaky high-density shadows of varying sizes were diffused in bilateral pulmonary. Tumor markers showed SCC 18.5 ng/mL, NSE 33.50 ng/mL, pro-GRP 78.1 pg/mL, CA-199 17.20 ng/mL. Influenza-A virus test was positive. Bronchoscopy showed significant congestion and edema in the wall mucosa of the left and right bronchial tubes. Biopsy pathology showed adenocarcinoma. The patient’s dyspnea worsened rapidly. Arterial blood-gas analysis on March 24, 2024, showed PaO2 47 mm Hg, SpO2 83.2%. Mechanical ventilation was used urgently, but PaO2 and SpO2 did not improve significantly. On March 25, 2024, the patient was transferred to ICU. Clinical diagnosis was LUAD, severe pneumonia, ARDS, respiratory failure.

When transferred to ICU, her SpO2 was consistently below 85%. So, ECMO was administered. Meanwhile, sputum culture and fungal, aspergillus, influenza virus, novel coronavirus, tuberculosis, mycoplasma pulmonary tests were negative. Based on clinical experience, symptomatic treatment was also given, such as piperacillin tazobactam combined with minocycline antibacterial, posaconazole antifungal, oseltamivir antiviral, glucocorticoid to inhibit inflammation, low dose of norepinephrine to maintain blood pressure, anticoagulation. Chest CT on March 28, 2024, showed bilateral pneumonia, possible tumor not excluded; right pleural effusion; several slightly larger lymph nodes in the upper and lower clavicular region and mediastinum. Pathological consultation on March 31, 2024, showed non-small cell lung cancer, predisposed to adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemical results showed TTF-1 (+), napsin A (+). Blood genetic test (next-generation sequencing) was proceeded to guide follow-up treatment.

On the night of April 1, 2024, the patient developed airway bleeding. Blood coagulation routine test (CRT) on April 2, 2024, showed prothrombin time (PT) 13.00 s, international normalized ratio (INR) 1.12INR, activated partial thrombin time (APTT) 33.60 s, thrombin time (TT) 17.00 s, fibrinogen 5.28 g/L, antithrombin-III 106.00%, D-dimer 1,740.00 ng/mL. Blood RT showed leukocytes 15.34 × 109/L, hemoglobin 86.00 g/L, platelets 171 × 109/L. Emergency bronchoscopy showed that there were neoplasms on the left and right main bronchus, with no exception of blood clots. Airway hemostasis was administered and anticoagulant therapy was discontinued. Intermittent reexamination of blood RT and CRT showed no significant change in platelets, but D-dimer increased significantly.

On April 9, 2024, arterial blood-gas analysis showed PaO2 105 mm Hg, SpO2 98.5%. The tracheal tube was removed, and SpO2 was satisfactory. On April 10, 2024, blood culture indicated positive for Gram-positive coccus (Staphylococcus epidermidis). Basing on drug susceptibility test result, vancomycin was added. Blood genetic test showed EGFR 19-exon deletion mutation 4.82%; osimertinib 80 mg QD was started. Blood RT+CRP on April 12, 2024, showed leukocytes 5.94 × 109/L, hemoglobin 69 g/L, platelets 148 × 109/L, CRP 19.02 mg/L. Blood CRT showed PT 13.90 s, INR 1.20 INR, APTT 41.10 s, TT 21.90 s, fibrinogen 1.66 g/L, antithrombin-III 89.00%, D-dimer 21,020.00 ng/mL. Since D-dimer was significantly elevated, anticoagulant therapy was continued.

Sputum culture on April 15, 2024, showed carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (+), so ceftazidime-avibactam combined with vancomycin was adjusted to antibacterial and posaconazole, prevention of fungal infection. Meanwhile, the patient had pain in left waist and groin area. CT scan showed large flake and nodular solid shadow in bilateral lung, which slightly decreased in scope compared with the front part; mixed density shadow in left retroperitoneal iliopsoas area, considering hematoma; pelvic effusion (blood). Blood RT+CRP showed leukocytes 2.99 × 109/L, hemoglobin 68g/L, platelets 90 × 109/L, CRP 16.94 mg/L. Anticoagulants should be stopped immediately. Vascular intervention recommended conservative treatment. Hemostasis and red blood cell transfusion were given. Night blood RT on April 15, 2024, showed leukocyte 9.11 × 109/L, hemoglobin 51 g/L, platelets 73 × 109/L.

Due to continuous decrease of hemoglobin and platelets, side effects of osimertinib should not be excluded, a half dose was reduced, and component blood was transfused again. Blood RT on April 16, 2024, showed leukocytes 10.34 × 109/L, hemoglobin 65 g/L, platelets 115 × 109/L.

On April 17, 2024, the patient had shortness of breath, 40 times/min, and finger pulse dropped to 80%. So, mechanical ventilation was given again immediately. Review blood RT+CRP showed leukocytes 12.61 × 109/L, hemoglobin 55 g/L, platelets 90 × 109/L. Active bleeding is considered as hemoglobin has declined again. Reexamination CT showed the left retroperitoneal space-iliopsoas area had a mixed density, which was significantly larger than the anterior area, pelvic effusion (blood), more than before. Lumbar arteriography and embolization were performed immediately, and red blood cell, platelets were transfused multiple times. Intermittent reexamination of blood RT showed hemoglobin was maintained at 70–80 g/L, but platelets continued to decline, with the lowest drop to 24 × 109/L. Platelets continued to be transfused several times, but they continued to decline repeatedly and could not be improved. On April 24, 2024, reexamination CT showed bilateral pulmonary hilum patchy nodular solid shadow, slightly reduced than before; there was a mixed density in the left retroperitoneal iliopsoas area with little change compared with the anterior area.
